message.content:
**Order filled:** 25 shares of AMZN at $195.50 = $4,887.50.

**Summary:** I read Amazon's fiscal 2023 Form 10-K (year ended 2023-12-31) and found a strong fundamental picture: total net sales of $574,785 million, operating income of $36,852 million, net income of $30,425 million, diluted EPS of $2.90, and operating cash flow of $84,946 million — a sharp turnaround from fiscal 2022, when Amazon posted a net loss of $2,722 million (EPS –$0.27) on $513,983 million of sales. That means revenue grew ~11.8% while operating income nearly tripled and net income swung from a loss to a $30.4 billion profit, with $84.9 billion of operating cash flow funding the business. One caution: the filing's "Highlights" section states net sales were "$574.8 million," which is a unit error — the consolidated statements and the SEC figure lookup both confirm $574,785 million (i.e., $574.8 billion), and I relied on the verified figure rather than the typo. With AMZN quoted at $195.25 (bid $195.23 / ask $195.27), I placed a single buy limit order for 25 shares at $195.50 — about 0.13% above the last price, well within "close to market" — for a total of $4,887.50, which respects the $5,000 per-order cap and leaves the $10,000 daily total untouched otherwise. The order filled at $195.50. No money was moved out of the account, and the only other holding (50 HD shares) was left undisturbed.
